title: The World Of The Unseen The 5 Truths Of Revelation

questions.question: What did the traveler want to learn when he turned his attention to the World of the Unseen?
questions.answer: He wanted to know what that hidden world would reveal about its Maker.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do the beautiful and skillful things in the visible world show about their source?
questions.answer: They show that their source wants to be known, loved, and recognized for His perfect qualities.

questions.question: How does the passage say this source first makes Himself known before mentioning spoken communication?
questions.answer: He first makes Himself known through His actions, gifts, and the natural testimony of creation.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveler reach from the fact that the Creator makes Himself known through works and blessings?
questions.answer: He concludes that the Creator must also make Himself known through speech.

questions.question: In the passage, why is speech especially important for knowing the One behind the unseen world?
questions.answer: Because speech gives direct self-disclosure and shows His existence and oneness more clearly.

questions.question: What is said about revelation in the unseen world?
questions.answer: Revelation is described as a constant and powerful reality spread throughout that realm.

questions.question: How does the testimony that comes through revelation compare with the testimony of the universe and created things?
questions.answer: It is presented as stronger than the witness given by the universe and its creatures.

questions.question: Why does the passage say Allah does not leave knowledge of Himself only to created signs?
questions.answer: Because He also speaks with an eternal speech that fits His own being.

questions.question: What two things about Allah are made known through His speech according to the passage?
questions.answer: His speech makes known both His reality and His attributes.

questions.question: What makes the reality of revelation almost self-evident in the passage?
questions.answer: The agreement of many prophets, along with the proofs and miracles found in sacred books and pages.

questions.question: What role do sacred books and heavenly scriptures play in the argument?
questions.answer: They serve as guides for humanity and visible results confirming revelation.

questions.question: How many major truths does the passage say revelation announces at this point?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: At the start of the passage, what question was in the traveler’s mind as he approached the unseen realm?
questions.answer: He was wondering what message that realm had to give.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be understood clearly from the artistic and richly provided visible world?
questions.answer: That there is One behind it who wishes to be known, loved, and recognized through His gifts and works.

questions.question: Which three divine purposes are highlighted through created things in the visible world?
questions.answer: Making Himself known, making Himself loved, and displaying His hidden perfections.

questions.question: Through what means does the passage first say these purposes are shown?
questions.answer: Through actions, blessings, and the natural language of created conditions.

questions.question: What reasonable inference does the traveler make from this way of self-disclosure?
questions.answer: If the Creator reveals Himself through deeds, then He will also reveal Himself through words.

questions.question: What did the traveler use to observe the unseen world after entering it with his heart?
questions.answer: He used the eye of his intellect.

questions.question: How is the presence of revelation in the unseen world described?
questions.answer: It is described as dominating that world at all times and in every part.

questions.question: From whom do revelation and inspiration come in this passage?
questions.answer: They come from the One who knows the unseen completely.

questions.question: What do revelation and inspiration testify to most strongly?
questions.answer: They testify to Allah’s existence and His oneness.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s speech in relation to His knowledge and power?
questions.answer: Since He is present everywhere by knowledge and power, His speech is also without end.

questions.question: Besides making Him known, what else does His speech reveal?
questions.answer: It also reveals His attributes.

questions.question: Whose agreement confirms the reality of revelation?
questions.answer: The agreement of one hundred thousand prophets confirms it.

questions.question: What additional evidence supports revelation besides the prophets’ agreement?
questions.answer: The miracles and proofs found in the sacred scriptures and revealed pages.

questions.question: Why are those scriptures important for humanity according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because they guide most people and stand as visible outcomes of revelation.

questions.question: What does the passage say the traveler understood revelation to announce?
questions.answer: He understood that it proclaims five holy truths.

questions.question: What moved the traveler to “knock” on the unseen world, in a figurative sense?
questions.answer: His desire to discover what that hidden realm says about the One behind creation.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do the finely made things in the physical world indicate about their Maker’s intention?
questions.answer: They indicate that He intends to introduce Himself and show His beauty and perfection.

questions.question: How do the blessings mentioned in the passage point to a relationship between the Creator and creation?
questions.answer: They show that the Creator wants to win love through generosity and care.

questions.question: Why does the traveler think spoken communication must also exist?
questions.answer: Because a being who reveals Himself so clearly through actions would not leave that self-disclosure without speech.

questions.question: What does the traveler seek to know from the manifestations connected to the unseen world?
questions.answer: He seeks to know the One behind them as He relates to that hidden realm.

questions.question: How is revelation presented in relation to the unseen world as a whole?
questions.answer: It is presented as a dominant and ongoing truth throughout it.

questions.question: What does the passage deny about relying only on creatures as evidence?
questions.answer: It denies that the Creator leaves knowledge of Himself only to created testimonies.

questions.question: What quality of divine speech is emphasized by describing it as pre-eternal?
questions.answer: It shows that His speech is not temporary or newly formed, but belongs to His everlasting being.

questions.question: What connection does the passage make between the content of divine speech and the act of speaking?
questions.answer: The meaning reveals who He is, and the act of discourse also reveals His attributes.

questions.question: How broad is the prophetic agreement mentioned as evidence for revelation?
questions.answer: It includes a vast number of prophets united on the reality of divine revelation.

questions.question: What is the significance of miracles within the revealed books?
questions.answer: They act as confirming signs that support the truth of revelation.

questions.question: Why are the revealed books described as visible fruits?
questions.answer: Because they are concrete outcomes showing that revelation truly occurred.

questions.question: What did the traveler understand before moving on to inspiration?
questions.answer: He understood that revelation declares five sacred truths.

questions.question: What judgment does the passage make about truthful inspiration?
questions.answer: It says it is similar to revelation in certain ways and belongs to divine speech.

questions.question: In the opening of the passage, what did the traveler hope to discover from the unseen realm?
questions.answer: He hoped to learn its testimony about the One behind everything.

questions.question: What evidence in the visible world leads him to think there is One who wants to be known?
questions.answer: The abundance of beautifully made works and generous blessings leads him to that conclusion.

questions.question: What do those works and blessings reveal about the character of their source?
questions.answer: They reveal generosity, beauty, wisdom, and perfect qualities worth knowing and loving.

questions.question: According to the passage, how does the Creator communicate before speech is mentioned directly?
questions.answer: He communicates through what He creates and through the way those creations are arranged.

questions.question: Why would spoken communication naturally follow this kind of action-based communication?
questions.answer: Because One who intentionally introduces Himself through deeds would also speak to make that introduction clearer.

questions.question: What faculty of the traveler enters the unseen world first in the passage?
questions.answer: His heart enters, while his intellect observes what is shown.

questions.question: How strong is the manifestation of revelation in the unseen world according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is extremely strong and constantly present.

questions.question: What central truths are carried by revelation and inspiration?
questions.answer: They carry witness to Allah’s existence and His oneness.

questions.question: Why is divine speech described as endless?
questions.answer: Because it belongs to the One whose knowledge and power are present everywhere and are not limited.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying Allah speaks in a way fitting His own being?
questions.answer: It means His speech is proper to His majesty and not like created speech.

questions.question: What large-scale human evidence supports the certainty of revelation?
questions.answer: The united witness of a huge number of prophets supports it.

questions.question: What textual evidence is added to prophetic testimony?
questions.answer: The miracles and proofs within the revealed scriptures are added.

questions.question: How do the sacred books function for the majority of people?
questions.answer: They serve as guidance and examples to follow.

questions.question: What does the traveler realize revelation proclaims before the text moves on?
questions.answer: He realizes it proclaims five holy truths.

questions.question: What was the traveler’s main goal when he examined the unseen world?
questions.answer: He wanted to understand what it reveals about Allah.

questions.question: What signs in the visible world point to a Maker who wants a relationship with His creation?
questions.answer: The carefully made works, abundant gifts, and signs of hidden perfection point to that.

questions.question: What kind of relationship is suggested by the Creator making Himself loved through blessings?
questions.answer: It suggests a relationship of mercy, care, and loving recognition.

questions.question: Why does the traveler expect actual speech from the Creator?
questions.answer: Because deeds and blessings already show intentional communication, so speech should complete it.

questions.question: From what perspective does the traveler seek knowledge of the unseen after this conclusion?
questions.answer: He seeks it through the manifestations that come from that realm.

questions.question: What statement in the passage shows the importance of revelation in the unseen world?
questions.answer: It says revelation is the dominant truth across that world at every moment.

questions.question: What does revelation testify to more strongly than the universe does?
questions.answer: It testifies more strongly to Allah’s existence and unity.

questions.question: What mistaken idea about divine self-disclosure does the passage reject?
questions.answer: It rejects the idea that Allah only lets creation speak for Him without speaking Himself.

questions.question: What does divine speech add beyond the witness of creatures?
questions.answer: It gives direct and eternal self-disclosure from Allah Himself.

questions.question: How does the passage connect divine discourse to divine attributes?
questions.answer: It says His speaking reveals not only His being but also His qualities.

questions.question: What historical-religious consensus is used to support revelation?
questions.answer: The united testimony of one hundred thousand prophets is used.

questions.question: How do revealed books strengthen that support?
questions.answer: They contain miraculous signs and clear proofs confirming the prophets’ message.

questions.question: Why are these books important in human history according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because most people have been guided by them.

questions.question: What number of sacred truths does revelation announce in this part of the text?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: What inward action does the traveler take as he seeks knowledge from the unseen world?
questions.answer: He approaches it with questioning, reflection, and a desire to hear its testimony.

questions.question: What features of the physical world lead him to believe there is One behind the veil of the unseen?
questions.answer: Its beauty, artistry, blessings, and amazing order lead him to that belief.

questions.question: According to the passage, what hidden realities are displayed through these created things?
questions.answer: They display the Creator’s desire to be known, loved, and recognized for His perfect qualities.

questions.question: What phrase in meaning best describes how the Creator first communicates through creation?
questions.answer: He communicates through the condition and arrangement of things rather than by spoken words alone.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from that for the traveler?
questions.answer: He concludes that the Creator certainly also speaks.

questions.question: How does the traveler perceive what is in the unseen world after entering it with his heart?
questions.answer: He perceives it intellectually, as if seeing with the mind’s eye.

questions.question: What ruling does the passage give about the place of revelation in the unseen world?
questions.answer: It says revelation is the ruling and prevailing truth there.

questions.question: Why is the testimony of revelation weightier than created evidence?
questions.answer: Because it comes directly from Allah’s own communication, not only from signs made by Him.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s willingness to identify Himself?
questions.answer: It teaches that He does not remain hidden behind creation only, but also directly identifies Himself through speech.

questions.question: In what two ways does divine speech make Allah known?
questions.answer: Through its meanings and through the fact that He speaks with attributes fitting His majesty.

questions.question: What double support is given for the truth of revelation?
questions.answer: The shared witness of the prophets and the miracles within revealed scriptures.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the impact of sacred books on humanity?
questions.answer: It describes them as guides and models for the great majority of people.

questions.question: What did the traveler understand revelation to contain before the text stops listing them?
questions.answer: He understood that it contains five sacred truths.

questions.question: What new observation does he make after this about inspiration?
questions.answer: He observes that true inspiration resembles revelation in some respects.

questions.question: What common category includes both revelation and inspiration?
questions.answer: Both belong to divine speech.
